source.author: lucan
source.text: Non Asiam brevioris aquae disterminat usquam Fluctus ab Europa, quamvis Byzantion arcto Pontus et ostriferam dirimat Chalcedona cursu, Euxinumque ferens parvo ruat ore Propontis.
source.text_original: Non Asiam brevioris aquae disterminat usquam / Fluctus ab Europa, quamvis Byzantion arcto / Pontus et ostriferam dirimat Chalcedona cursu, / Euxinumque ferens parvo ruat ore Propontis.
source.text_english: No wave of the narrower waters separates Asia from Europe anywhere, though the Pontus divides Byzantium from narrow strait and Chalcedon rich in oysters, and the Propontis, bearing the Euxine, rushes through a small mouth.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: insurgit transtris et remo Nerea versat Canthus, in Aeaeo volvet quem barbara cuspis pulvere; at interea clari decus adiacet orbis, quem genitor gestabat Abas: secat aurea fluctu tegmina Chalcidicas fugiens Euripus harenas, celsaque semiferum contorquens frena luporum surgis ab ostrifero medius, Neptune, Geraesto.
reuse.text_original: insurgit transtris et remo Nerea versat / Canthus, in Aeaeo volvet quem barbara cuspis / pulvere; at interea clari decus adiacet orbis, / quem genitor gestabat Abas: secat aurea fluctu / tegmina Chalcidicas fugiens Euripus harenas, / celsaque semiferum contorquens frena luporum / surgis ab ostrifero medius, Neptune, Geraesto.
reuse.text_english: Canthus rises up on the rowing benches and turns Nereus with his oar, whom the barbarian spear will roll in Aeaean dust; but meanwhile there lies the glory of the shining sphere, which his father Abas had borne: the golden Euripus, fleeing from the waves, cuts through the sands of Chalcis, and you rise, Neptune, high in the middle of ostrich-bearing Geraestus, hurling the lofty reins of the half-wolf creatures.
